newsitem.title: COTE D'IVOIRE: Abidjan bourse ends modestly higher on week.
newsitem.headline: Abidjan bourse ends modestly higher on week.

text.p: The Abidjan bourse edged higher again this week though volume remained low, according to the bourse report.
The BVA index added 0.28 percent to 492.79, leaving it 37.7 percent higher than at the start of the year.

As last week, volume was exaggerated by a block trade in the shares of SIEM, Ivory Coast's main producer of cans and metal packaging. The government's 10 percent stake was floated on the bourse last month.

A bourse official said the block trades involved shares that were sold to SIEM employees at the flotation price of 29,500 CFA francs, which is still the market price. For technical reasons, the transfer to employees had not been possible before the flotation, she said.
Elsewhere, shares in electricity company CIE were 870 CFA francs lower at 20,410, adjusted for a dividend payment of 860 CFA francs.
Among the gainers were rubber company SOGB, up 750 CFA francs at 17,600, and civil engineering firm SETAO, which rose 980 to 17,600.
